## Codex Critic Verdict — REVISE

### MAJOR

**[The safe-open contract overclaims Linux guarantees]** — Plan §§D2/D4 claim the helper opens “without following symlinks and without ever blocking.” Linux `open(2)` says `O_NOFOLLOW` protects only the trailing component; earlier symlinked components are followed. `fstat(fd)` verifies the opened inode’s type but does not detect parent substitution or replacement of the pathname after opening. Linux also states `O_NONBLOCK` has no effect for regular files and does not impose a wall-clock bound on their `open()`. Merely constructing the deadline first therefore cannot interrupt a stalled open, and the existing loops attempt `flock` before checking expiry, allowing acquisition after the deadline. Plan §D4 additionally admits sites 1 and 3 have no caller deadline, leaving the binding body `## Acceptance` bullet 1 unsatisfied. Finally, `_REJECTION_ERRNOS` includes `EAGAIN`; on Linux, `EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK` can mean an incompatible lease on a regular file, so wrapping it as a special-path `LockPathError` changes the fail-closed callers’ exit handling. Revise the contract and implementation to enforce the required bound, preserve non-special errors, and either secure parent traversal or explicitly narrow the acceptance claim and record that residual. `mechanizable: yes` — test a symlinked parent, injected `EAGAIN`, and a delayed open that extends beyond the deadline; assert no post-deadline acquisition and the intended exception/exit contract.

**[Signal lock mode can be paired with stale attempt state]** — On `origin/issue-2323`, `_active_job_id` is assigned at `scripts/codex_task.py:1355` but never cleared before retries (`:1924–1953`). Plan §D6 overwrites `_active_lock_mode` immediately before the next spawn while retaining that previous job ID. A signal during the next lock acquisition or spawn can therefore post a marker naming the prior job with either the prior or new attempt’s lock mode. The proposed signal test manually seeds globals, so it cannot catch this integration defect. Reset or update the active job/mode as one coherent attempt state before each retry, and exercise the real signal timing around a second attempt. `mechanizable: yes` — complete one attempt, enter a retry, invoke the captured handler before the new job ID assignment, and assert it cannot emit a stale-job/new-mode pairing.

**[Leg A-only completion violates binding acceptance]** — `origin/main:scripts/codex_task.py` has no `_dispatch_lock`, while `git show origin/issue-2323:scripts/codex_task.py` confirms it at line 1221. Plan §D5 nevertheless permits completing #2324 with Leg A alone if #2323 never merges. The body’s `## Acceptance` bullets unconditionally require the Codex lock hardening and `dispatch_lock=<mode>` on all post-lock failure paths; a completion note declaring them N/A does not satisfy those criteria. Keep #2324 open, formally re-scope its binding acceptance, or terminate it as superseded—do not mark the stated task complete with Leg B absent. `mechanizable: yes` — gate completion on `_dispatch_lock` being present on `main` and the Leg B failure-note tests passing.

**[The child-process regression matrix is incomplete]** — Body `## Acceptance` bullet 3 requires FIFO and symlink fixtures in a child process with bounded completion per site. Plan §6 does this for both `sync_repo_root.py` opens, but specifies only the FIFO arm in a child for `step9c_baseline.py`, and only the FIFO arm in a child for `_dispatch_lock`; their symlink cases remain in-process. Amend the matrix so both fixture classes execute under a subprocess timeout at every named site, with asserted outcome and exit posture. `mechanizable: yes` — parameterize `(site, fixture_kind)` and require every case to return before the timeout with the exact D3 posture.

**What’s sound:** The named functions, handlers, and branch-only failure paths all exist as grounded; `cmd_refresh` is a valid place to add the proposed catch; the existing Codex `except OSError` preserves its fail-open `unavailable` mode; clearing `O_NONBLOCK` is harmless for these later uses; Leg A has zero file overlap with #2323; the same-tree helper loader is compatible with `step9c_baseline.py`’s import discipline; and the scope inventory and smoke-blind-spot declaration are sound. The `scripts/foo.py` verifier residue is illustrative rather than load-bearing.
